question: Did task2592's registered held-out root selector produce mutually unique evaluation histories and zero overlap with the roots actually used by its generic training games?

scope.operation: Reconstruct exactly those registered four-ply family roots from the frozen task2592 rules; compare canonical full-history records for uniqueness within each rule and against initial_record values actually present in the corresponding generic training games.jsonl.
scope.forbidden: Do not read W/L outcomes, scores, learner weights or evaluation game logs; do not select different families; do not regenerate rules, rerun fitness or modify task2592/task2595 results.

decision.pass: All eight registered EVAL histories are unique within each rule and none equals any actual TRAIN initial history for the same rule.
decision.fail: Report exact duplicate and overlap counts per rule. A structural failure only; it does not invalidate task2592 W/L outcomes, but narrows the independence claim and requires a corrected pre-registration before any new reuse.

cost: Read-only local processing of one existing 9.1 MB training record file and 32 existing root constructions; expected under 2 minutes.
